whyItMatters: Broad and external ACL grants are the highest-risk ACL changes because they can immediately expose data or preserve access for another principal outside the normal policy path.

threatContext.attackerBehavior: An attacker may grant access to the `AllUsers` or `AuthenticatedUsers` groups, or to a separate AWS account they control, to preserve access or stage exfiltration.
threatContext.realWorldUsage: This is attractive in legacy ACL-enabled environments where exposure can be created quickly without editing bucket policy.
threatContext.whyItMatters: The grant scope is the real security signal: public, authenticated, or external-account exposure should be handled as a top-priority S3 event.
threatContext.riskAndImpact: If missed, defenders may fail to detect direct data exposure or external persistence introduced through ACLs.

requiredLogSources: AWS CloudTrail for S3 ACL operations
loggingRequirements: CloudTrail must preserve canned ACLs and structured grant payloads where possible.
The environment should parse S3 grantee groups and canonical-user or account grants.
ACL-effectiveness context should be available to avoid over-alerting on disabled ACL targets.
limitations: Structured grant details may be difficult to query directly depending on storage format.
Some legacy workflows may legitimately share data cross-account.
Canned ACL text alone does not capture every nuanced grantee relationship.

enrichment.description: Resolve whether the ACL created public, authenticated-user, or external-account access.
enrichment.falsePositiveReduction: Makes broad exposure explicit instead of inferring from raw text only.

enrichment.description: Determine whether the specific grantee or exposure class is approved for the target.
enrichment.falsePositiveReduction: Separates legitimate sharing from suspicious exposure.

enrichment.description: Classify the exposed bucket or object by business sensitivity.
enrichment.falsePositiveReduction: Improves prioritization of risky ACL grants.

logicExplanation.humanReadable: This rule should detect ACL changes that create broad or external exposure. It should parse canned ACLs and structured grants to identify public, authenticated-user, or external-account access on ACL-effective targets.
conditions: ACL result resolves to public, authenticated-users, or external-account access
target still honors ACLs where that context is available
logicExplanation.tuningGuidance: 1. Parse grant scope explicitly. 2. Maintain approved-sharing inventories for known partner accounts. 3. Escalate strongly for public exposure or sensitive data targets.
logicExplanation.whenToFire: Fire when an ACL change grants broad or external access to a bucket or object.

deployment.scheduling: Real-time is preferred because broad ACL grants can expose data immediately.
considerations: This is the grant-scope branch of the S3 ACL family.
Grant parsing and approved-sharing inventories are the main dependencies.
